title: Netflix Sets 'Dilwali Diwali' for November 5 With Mihir Ahuja, Manoj Pahwa
excerpt: The Terribly Tiny Tales family drama follows a son who returns from abroad for Diwali with a new apartment for his parents — and learns a house is not a home. It streams globally on Netflix on 5 November.
body:
• Netflix has announced 'Dilwali Diwali', a family drama starring Mihir Ahuja and Manoj Pahwa, premiering worldwide on the platform on 5 November 2026.
  • Mihir Ahuja plays Ansh Sikka, who returns home for Diwali after years working abroad, having bought his middle-class Punjabi parents a new high-rise apartment.
  • The film is produced by Terribly Tiny Tales, written by Ritu Mago and directed by Ritesh Menon, and also stars Neelu Kohli and Aurra Bhatnagar.
  • Diaspora viewers can watch it on Netflix from 5 November — it streams globally on the same day, no separate India release window.

Netflix has announced a new Hindi family film, Dilwali Diwali, which will premiere on the platform on 5 November 2026. The film stars Mihir Ahuja and Manoj Pahwa, with Neelu Kohli and Aurra Bhatnagar in supporting roles, and was announced by the makers on Monday, according to Cinema Express.

Produced by Terribly Tiny Tales (TTT), written by Ritu Mago and directed by Ritesh Menon, the film is a festive family drama about what 'home' means when a child's idea of a better life collides with a parent's. It marks another collaboration between TTT and Netflix after Greater Kalesh and Musafir Cafe, Bollywood Hungama reported.

A house upgrade that is not a home upgrade

Mihir Ahuja plays Ansh Sikka, a young man who has done what many children dream of doing for their parents: giving them a better life. After years of working abroad, he has bought his middle-class Punjabi parents a swanky new high-rise apartment, complete with every comfort of an upgraded address. But when he returns home for Diwali, he discovers that a new home does not necessarily mean a fresh start.

"Giving your parents a house upgrade is one thing; getting them to upgrade their idea of home is quite another," the makers' press note reads. As the Sikka family comes together for the festival, their differing ideas of what makes a good life spark moments of humour, tenderness and recognition — the parents remain attached to the memories and familiarity of their old life while Ansh measures love in square footage and amenities.

"For a parent, home is never just about the walls, the furniture, or the address. It's about the memories you've built, the people you've shared your life with, and the little things that make a place your own."

— Manoj Pahwa, who plays Ansh's father

The cast on the story

Mihir Ahuja, who leads the film as Ansh, said the character's journey "comes from a place of love. I think that's what makes the story so relatable. We all want to do the best for our families, but sometimes, in trying to give them more, we forget to understand what truly makes them happy." Manoj Pahwa added that children and parents may have different ideas of a good life, "but the love behind both perspectives is the same," in comments reported by IANS.

A story built for the diaspora's Diwali

The premise — a son working abroad who flies home for Diwali carrying a grand gesture, and learns the gesture missed the point — is drawn directly from the NRI experience. Ansh is not a visitor in his own family; he is the family's success story, and the film's tension comes from the gap between providing for parents from a distance and understanding them up close.

For diaspora viewers, the practical details are simple: Dilwali Diwali premieres on Netflix on 5 November 2026 and will be available to subscribers worldwide on the same day, including in the US, Canada, the UK, the UAE and Australia. No trailer had been released with the announcement at the time of writing; the film was unveiled with a poster and the makers' press note.
